verdict.rationale: Better Auth is code-first rather than dashboard-driven: its configuration lives in code, server-side `auth.api` methods and client methods cover authentication, and the admin plugin exposes user management operations (create users, manage roles, ban, impersonate). That means the operations are inherently available programmatically, but there is no documented statement of full parity with any UI. Community reports say running admin scripts was hacky because of the request-header design, no published OpenAPI spec was found, and there is no guidance on writing non-JS clients. Missing for 10: an explicit API-vs-UI parity guarantee, a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI), smooth headless/scripted admin usage, and independent corroboration of complete programmatic coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: No dashboard clicks. Your auth lives in code version controlled, type-safe, and reviewable in PRs.
To authenticate a user on the server, you can use the `auth.api` methods.
It allows administrators to perform various operations such as creating users, managing user roles, banning/unbanning users, impersonating users, and more.
